v11.82 - a-17 ilk yarı: orkestrasyon gözlediğini kaydediyor, hiçbir karar fiyata bakmıyor

A finished run knows something a run about to start does not: which SHAPE of
approach was taken, and what came of it. That is kept now — and ONLY that.

WHAT IS STORED (`src/core/missionOutcomes.ts`, new)

  · a strategy SIGNATURE — the ordered primitives the lead used with consecutive
    repeats collapsed, plus the features of the approach (branching, replan,
    revision, review, conversation, council, workflow, nested, human). The
    collapse is the whole design: without it every run has its own signature,
    nothing ever aggregates, and the feature looks like it works while answering
    nothing. How BIG it was is `counts`, which is a different question.
  · the verdict, the stop reason, how many REQUIRED criteria a current
    evaluation actually put at pass, the counts, the duration, the money.
  · NOT one prompt, artefact, message body or agent's words. This is not a
    second memory; every one of those already has a source of truth.

THE FENCES ARE THE FEATURE

  · a group under the sample floor is REPORTED (hiding it would be its own lie)
    and marked `enough: false`, and is NEVER briefed to a lead. A lead told
    "this approach succeeded" on one run treats it as settled and stops looking.
  · the classic-vs-adaptive comparison is refused while either side lacks a
    denominator, and says which side is short rather than implying they are
    equal.
  · a project never sees another's runs, and "no project" is a SCOPE, not a
    wildcard that matches every project on the machine.
  · what the lead is handed is evidence phrased as observation, with the
    briefing itself saying it is a record and not a recommendation — a
    recommendation dressed as data is how a runtime planner becomes a lookup
    table.

AND COST DECIDES NOTHING. No cheap-first, no model escalation or de-escalation,
no budget reserve, no expected-value stop. A price here is a fact about what
happened. That is a promise about what the code does NOT do, so no fixture can
show it and the test reads it off the source instead.

PERSISTENCE, RESTATED BECAUSE A NEW STORE DOES NOT INHERIT IT: missing is not
corrupt (X-62), syntax is not schema (X-87), a file from the future is read-only
(X-64), the write is atomic and a failed rename NEVER falls back to a direct one.
A separate file from missions.json on purpose — the mission store rolls old runs
out and the point of a history is that it survives that.

Recording walks every terminal run and is keyed on the run id, so it is
idempotent: a run that ended in another window, or whose verdict was corrected,
is picked up by the same pass, and the first run of this code records every
mission the farm has ever finished — which is the migration. A rerun is a
different run id and counts separately, because it is a second attempt.

Built from the RUN RECORD, never the journal: a trace can be deleted, truncated
or damaged, and a measurement that fell over when it was would be unreliable
exactly on the runs that went worst.

Readable through `missions.outcomes`.

‼️ HALF THE ITEM IS OPEN and A-17 is NOT closed. The Missions page has no
surface for this yet, and whether deleting a run should also forget its outcome
is an unmade decision — `MissionOutcomeStore.forget` exists and is deliberately
unwired. See the handover note.

Measured in test/test_mission_outcomes.js (new, 71). 14110 tests pass.
